title.zh: 维护种族和谐（文件送达）条例 2026
title.en: Maintenance of Racial Harmony (Service of Documents) Regulations 2026

completenessNote: 全文，共 8 条；逐字取自新加坡法规在线（SSO）官方打印视图，未改写、未节选。

text.en: 1. These Regulations are the Maintenance of Racial Harmony (Service of Documents) Regulations 2026 and come into operation on 15 September 2026.

3.—(1) Parts 2 and 3 apply in relation to a document permitted or required by or under the Act to be served on a person if, and only if, no method for serving that document is expressly prescribed under the Act.
(2) Part 4 applies in relation to any document permitted or required by or under the Act to be served on a person.
(3) These Regulations do not apply for the purposes of court proceedings.

heading.en: Service of documents on partnership other than limited liability partnership

text.en:
5. A document to be served on a partnership (other than a limited liability partnership) may be served —
(a)by giving it to any partner or other similar officer, or an authorised representative, of the partnership;
(b)by leaving it at, or by sending it by registered post to, the partnership’s business address; or
(c)by sending it by fax to the fax number used at the partnership’s business address.

heading.en: Service of documents on body corporate or unincorporated association

text.en:
6. A document to be served on a body corporate (including a limited liability partnership) or an unincorporated association may be served —
(a)by giving it to the secretary or other similar officer of the body corporate or unincorporated association, or the limited liability partnership’s manager;
(b)by leaving it at, or by sending it by registered post to, the registered office or principal office in Singapore of the body corporate or unincorporated association; or
(c)by sending it by fax to the fax number used at the registered office or principal office in Singapore of the body corporate or unincorporated association.

heading.en: Additional modes of service of document

text.en:
7.—(1) In addition, a document to be served on a person (X) may be served —
(a)by sending it by email to X’s last email address;
(b)by sending an electronic notice to X using X’s chosen means of notification, stating —
(i)that the document is available; and
(ii)how X may use X’s chosen means of access to access the document’s contents; or
(c)if the Minister or the competent authority is serving the document on X and X’s name cannot be ascertained despite the exercise of reasonable diligence —
(i)by posting the document on a website maintained by the competent authority and specified by the Minister for this purpose; or
(ii)by sending an electronic copy of the document to an account on social media associated with X, if the account provides a mechanism for X to receive electronic communications in that account.
(2) However, a method of service mentioned in paragraph (1)(a) or (b) may only be used if X gives prior written consent for service by that method.
